Project.name: grace-tma-platform
Project.annotation: Scalable Telegram Mini App platform with bot assistant, Fastify backend, and protected CRM for rehabilitation and conversion-retention workflows with a calm medical iOS-glass experience layer.
Project.keywords: telegram mini app, bot, fastify, prisma, postgresql, crm, subscriptions, movecoins, diagnostics, medical safety, conversion funnel, campaign automation, ios glass, medical minimalism

Actors.actor-Patient: User interacting via Telegram bot and Mini App for diagnostics and exercises.
Actors.actor-Operator: CRM manager handling subscriptions, escalations, and content operations.
Actors.actor-System: Automated backend services for billing gates, rewards, analytics, and notifications.

UC-001.Action: Starts from bot and opens Mini App through deep link
UC-001.Goal: Complete onboarding with first diagnostic and first training
UC-001.Preconditions: Telegram account is available and backend can validate initData
UC-001.AcceptanceCriteria: Diagnostic is saved, onboarding reward +20 MoveCoins is recorded once, first training is available

UC-002.Action: Completes diagnostic wizard with zone, VAS score, symptoms, and red flags
UC-002.Goal: Receive safe and personalized access to exercise content
UC-002.Preconditions: User is authenticated and diagnostic questionnaire version is active
UC-002.AcceptanceCriteria: Diagnostic record exists, computed mobility index is updated, safety gate is evaluated server-side

UC-003.Action: Completes exercise session or sharing action
UC-003.Goal: Earn MoveCoins and spend them on premium courses or merchandise
UC-003.Preconditions: Exercise session is eligible and anti-fraud checks pass
UC-003.AcceptanceCriteria: Accrual/debit transactions are logged idempotently and user balance remains non-negative

UC-004.Action: Checks subscription status on each Mini App entry
UC-004.Goal: Apply access policy by subscription stage
UC-004.Preconditions: User has a subscription record or defaults to trial policy
UC-004.AcceptanceCriteria: Expired users are blocked from heavy level and receive renewal prompt while active users retain full access

UC-005.Goal: Block unsafe training and escalate to CRM/doctor queue
UC-005.Preconditions: Diagnostic submission contains red flag criteria matched by server rules
UC-005.AcceptanceCriteria: Training lock is enabled immediately, escalation task is created with SLA metadata, and user receives safe guidance

UC-006.Action: Manages users, subscriptions, bonuses, and diagnostic history in CRM
UC-006.Goal: Operate retention and medical escalation workflows without engineering intervention
UC-006.Preconditions: Operator is authenticated with role-based access
UC-006.AcceptanceCriteria: Operator can search by TG_ID, inspect history, update subscription access, and issue bonus MoveCoins with audit logs

UC-007.Action: Updates exercise media and diagnostic text content from CRM
UC-007.Goal: Publish content changes without rebuilding client applications
UC-007.Preconditions: Content passes validation and storage upload policies
UC-007.AcceptanceCriteria: Updated content is visible in TMA/Bot immediately through API-backed catalogs

UC-008.Action: Sends trigger-based notifications and inline progress cards in bot
UC-008.Preconditions: User has notification consent and event triggers are emitted
UC-008.AcceptanceCriteria: Reminder, weekly summary, and reward messages are delivered with retry/backoff policies and can render inline cards

UC-009.Action: Runs timed conversion campaigns with deadline windows and personalized offer steps
UC-009.Goal: Convert trial and inactive users to paid plans without manual operator work
UC-009.Preconditions: User belongs to campaign segment and consent/policy checks pass
UC-009.AcceptanceCriteria: Campaign steps are delivered in configured sequence, countdown messages remain time-consistent, and conversion outcomes are tracked

UC-010.Action: Manages campaign copy, promo windows, and support escalation scripts in CRM
UC-010.Goal: Tune commercial funnel and support quality without deployment cycles
UC-010.AcceptanceCriteria: Operator can publish offer waves, cap reminder frequency, and activate support scripts with full audit trail

UC-011.Action: Advances user campaign state through finite steps (entry, nurture, urgency, last_call, convert)
UC-011.Goal: Orchestrate deterministic conversion flow with replay-safe transitions
UC-011.Preconditions: User is enrolled into campaign and transition policy allows next step
UC-011.AcceptanceCriteria: Only one valid transition is accepted per step key, duplicate events are ignored, and state history is auditable

UC-012.Action: Suppresses campaign messaging for red-flag users and reroutes to support-safe communication
UC-012.Goal: Guarantee that medical risk users never receive urgency sales pressure
UC-012.Preconditions: User has active red-flag lock or unresolved medical escalation
UC-012.AcceptanceCriteria: Campaign sends are blocked, suppression reason is logged, and support/clinical message path is used instead

UC-013.Action: Executes high-conversion campaign script with bounded urgency windows similar to proven Telegram fitness funnels
UC-013.Goal: Maintain strong conversion while preserving trust and medical-safe communication boundaries
UC-013.Preconditions: User is eligible for campaign segment and has no active medical suppression state
UC-013.AcceptanceCriteria: Flow follows deterministic script (entry, social proof, value reminder, urgency, last-call) with measurable conversion per step

UC-014.Action: Uses Mini App and bot interfaces styled in medical minimal iOS glass design language
UC-014.Goal: Receive calm, premium, and readable UX that reduces anxiety and friction
UC-014.Preconditions: Client supports modern CSS features for blur/transparency with accessible fallbacks
UC-014.AcceptanceCriteria: Primary user journeys are fully usable with glass surfaces, clear contrast, tactile hierarchy, and no noisy visual overload

UC-015.Action: Resolves localized content and interface language across TMA, Bot, and Backend for ru/en/xx
UC-015.Goal: Deliver consistent multilingual UX and localized medical content
UC-015.Preconditions: Supported locale list and fallback order are configured
UC-015.AcceptanceCriteria: API returns localized exercises/questions by Accept-Language or user preference, and TMA/Bot strings match resolved locale

UC-016.Action: Triggers Panic Button from exercise screen
UC-016.Goal: Instantly escalate to operator for urgent support path
UC-016.Preconditions: User is in active exercise context and session is authenticated
UC-016.AcceptanceCriteria: Panic action creates immediate UC-005 escalation event, notifies operator channel/CRM queue, and locks high-risk flows pending review

UC-017.Action: Wraps MoveCoins mutations in transaction with actionId-based idempotency key
UC-017.Goal: Prevent double accrual/debit and maintain ledger integrity
UC-017.Preconditions: actionId is present for each reward/spend request
UC-017.AcceptanceCriteria: Duplicate actionId requests are no-op safe, balance invariants remain valid, and transaction logs are auditable

ExperienceGuidelines.guideline-1: Visual language is calm medical minimalism: restrained palette, spacious layout, reduced cognitive load.
ExperienceGuidelines.guideline-2: Glass surfaces use subtle blur and translucency inspired by iOS glass, but preserve readability and accessibility.
ExperienceGuidelines.guideline-3: Urgency blocks in conversion funnels must remain ethical: no deceptive countdown resets or contradictory deadlines.
ExperienceGuidelines.guideline-4: All critical actions (start training, renew, contact support, escalate) remain one-tap and visually prominent.
ExperienceGuidelines.guideline-5: Red-flag and medical-safe messages always override sales or promo visuals in hierarchy and timing.

NonGoals.item-1: No native iOS/Android app in v1; Telegram surfaces are primary channels.
NonGoals.item-2: No direct diagnostic advice generation by LLM without clinical guardrails and curated answers.
NonGoals.item-3: No multi-region active-active deployment in first release.
NonGoals.item-4: No replacement of licensed medical consultation by automated bot recommendations.

Constraints.constraint-1: Server-side safety checks are mandatory for red-flag outcomes; client-only checks are insufficient.
Constraints.constraint-2: Medical and personal data must be protected via strict RBAC and data-minimizing logs.
Constraints.constraint-3: All MoveCoins mutations must be transactional, auditable, and idempotent.
Constraints.constraint-4: Subscription access rules are enforced on every protected API call and TMA entry.
Constraints.constraint-5: Media access uses signed URLs with expiration; no unrestricted public links for protected assets.
Constraints.constraint-6: Telegram API and webhook reliability must include queueing, retries, and backoff.
Constraints.constraint-7: Campaign countdown and urgency messages must be generated from server time to avoid inconsistent or misleading deadlines.
Constraints.constraint-8: Notification cadence must enforce anti-spam limits per user and per campaign stage.
Constraints.constraint-9: Users with active red-flag status are excluded from urgency and conversion campaign steps until medical unlock.
Constraints.constraint-10: Campaign state transitions must be idempotent and monotonic per enrollment timeline.
Constraints.constraint-11: Design system must implement iOS-glass-inspired components with accessibility-safe contrast and fallback styles for low-support devices.
Constraints.constraint-12: Campaign urgency text must use one canonical server deadline source and cannot silently restart expired countdowns.
Constraints.constraint-13: Localization fallback order is strict: explicit user preference, Accept-Language match, default locale.
Constraints.constraint-14: Campaign sends and conversion steps are blocked when medicalStatus indicates red-flag suppression state.
Constraints.constraint-15: Panic Button must be one-tap reachable in exercise UI and never hidden behind secondary navigation.
Constraints.constraint-16: Every MoveCoins mutation requires actionId and executes in a Prisma transaction boundary.

Risks.risk-1: False negatives in red-flag detection can expose users to unsafe exercise recommendations.
Risks.risk-2: Duplicate event processing may produce incorrect MoveCoins balances without strong idempotency keys.
Risks.risk-3: CRM over-permissioning can leak sensitive history if role policy is weak.
Risks.risk-4: Notification spikes can exceed Telegram throughput limits and degrade delivery quality.
Risks.risk-5: Subscription state drift between payment callbacks and access checks can lock out active users.
Risks.risk-6: Aggressive campaign cadence can increase churn, complaints, or Telegram abuse reports.
Risks.risk-7: Countdown/promo mismatch between bot copy and backend state can reduce trust and legal compliance.
Risks.risk-8: Invalid campaign step transitions may create loops, duplicate sends, or broken attribution.
Risks.risk-9: Missing red-flag suppression in conversion flows can create clinical and reputational incidents.
Risks.risk-10: Overuse of glass effects may reduce readability or performance on low-end devices if fallback policy is weak.
Risks.risk-11: Aggressive conversion copy can conflict with clinical tone and reduce long-term trust.
Risks.risk-12: Locale mismatch between bot, TMA, and API can produce mixed-language user journeys.
Risks.risk-13: Missing suppression check in campaign path can send notifications to medically blocked users.
Risks.risk-14: Absent idempotency enforcement in MoveCoins flow can cause balance drift under retries.

OpenQuestions.question-1: Which payment providers and webhook contracts are used for subscription lifecycle events?
OpenQuestions.question-2: What SLA and escalation routing should apply for red-flag cases by severity level?
OpenQuestions.question-3: What retention window applies to diagnostic records and media under compliance policy?
OpenQuestions.question-4: Should AI concierge responses be fully canned from approved FAQ or allow constrained generation with moderation?
OpenQuestions.question-5: What legal and policy constraints apply to urgency offers, discounts, and campaign copy in target jurisdictions?
OpenQuestions.question-6: What maximum daily campaign-contact limit is acceptable before user fatigue increases materially?
OpenQuestions.question-7: What criteria unlock a red-flag user back into eligible campaign segments?
OpenQuestions.question-8: What attribution model is canonical for conversion (first-touch, last-touch, or weighted multi-touch)?
